title: Reproduce AgentTune's AI Personality Studies & Datasets
description: Download frozen responses, questionnaires, and zero-dependency Node/Python scripts to reproduce all 10,000 Nov 2026 sheets, Sept 2026 cohorts, and Wave 3 PCA.
h1: How to reproduce AgentTune’s AI self-report research
lede: Every score in our November 2026 and September 2026 studies is computed from frozen raw answer files stored right in the repository. You can download those JSON and CSV files and re-run the exact scoring scripts on your own machine in under a minute with Node.js and Python—no API key, model call, or npm install needed.
answer: Download the frozen JSON and CSV files from /research/data/, then run 'node september-2026-score.cjs' and 'node content-analysis.cjs' to verify the 2,003-record September archive, or run 'python3 tools/analyze-psychometric-forensics.py' to recompute the 10,000-sheet November dataset (including the 63.58% single-factor PCA, Campbell-Fiske MTMM matrix, and 0.054 to 1.499 bits Shannon entropy) at $0.00 API cost.

sections.html: These scripts recompute scores from our frozen September 24, 2026 answer vectors and numeric scoring keys. All 2,003 raw integer vectors and numerical summaries are preserved intact (see the provenance note and current open tests).

Save these five files into the same directory without renaming them: responses, instruments, original scorer, extended analysis, and protocols. Run both scripts with Node.js (zero npm dependencies):

node september-2026-score.cjs > my-summary.json
node content-analysis.cjs > my-analysis.json

Compare your generated files against the published summary.json and content-analysis.json.

Each record in september-2026-responses.json contains model, administration, test, and an ordered integer answers array (plus optional 1-based inapplicable_items flags).

The file holds 2,003 records: 2,000 fresh-session vectors across four models (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1) plus 3 canonical vectors for Grok 4.6. Note that Astra and Sol ran all five tests per fresh session (100 sessions each), while Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 ran one test per fresh session (500 sessions each).

sections.h2: Verify provenance before changing a file
sections.html: In the website repository, running node tools/build-content-analysis.js rebuilds all JSON and CSV summaries and verifies cohort sizes, tie counts, midpoint rates, and item-level differences.

sections.h2: Make a result table others can interpret
sections.html: When citing or extending these results, state the model cohort, instrument, sample size (fresh sessions vs simulated draws), and tie-breaking rule. Saying “100 of 100 runs scored Secure on the ECR-R scale” is an exact, reproducible statement; saying “this model forms secure human attachments” is not.

faq.q: Do I need an OpenRouter or OpenAI API key to reproduce these results?
faq.a: No. All 10,000 November 2026 response sheets and 2,003 September 2026 response vectors are frozen in the repository under /research/data/, so running the Node.js and Python scoring scripts costs $0.00 and makes zero network calls.

faq.q: Which script recomputes the Big One PCA (63.58% PC1) and Shannon item entropy?
faq.a: Run python3 tools/analyze-psychometric-forensics.py from the repository root to deterministically recompute the 10,000-sheet Jacobi PCA eigenvalues, Campbell-Fiske MTMM correlation matrix, Miller-Madow / Shannon item entropy (0.054 to 1.499 bits), and 50-item embodiment statistics.

faq.q: How are tied scores handled when re-scoring the frozen response vectors?
faq.a: Both september-2026-score.cjs and our browser scorer (resources/scoring/score.js) report legacy tie-broken counts alongside tie-preserving results (marking tied MBTI axes as X and listing all tied top DISC and Enneagram types openly).
